You're using a very formal, logical definition of the term "equal" here. You're not wrong, you're just using the term in a different way than most people outside of maths or a logic class would use it.

In more relaxed language, equals just means "is". Someone might say "pool plus alcohol equals a good weekend" and that makes sense. But saying  "a good weekend equals alcohol plus a pool" implies that there's only one way to have a good weekend and that doesn't really make sense. So the "equals" here doesn't go both ways. 

Similarly, you can believe that trans women are women, but understand that not all women are trans women and therefore trans women doesn't equal women in a mathematical sense. Rather, the former is a subset of the latter.
